sections.title: Part 1 · Listening to Problem Solving
sections.instructions: Listen to the conversation and answer the questions.
sections.passage:
AGENT: Good morning, Maple Grove Property Management, this is Dana.
CUSTOMER: Hi, this is Sam in unit 402. My heating stopped working last night.
AGENT: I'm sorry to hear that. When exactly did it stop?
CUSTOMER: Around nine o'clock. I noticed the apartment getting cold.
AGENT: Have you checked the thermostat and the breaker panel?
CUSTOMER: Yes. The thermostat is set to twenty-four, and all the breakers look fine.
AGENT: I'll send a technician this afternoon. They should arrive by two.
CUSTOMER: I have a meeting until four. Could they come after that?
AGENT: Of course. I'll book the visit for four thirty.
CUSTOMER: Great, thank you for your help.

SPEAKER A: I believe working from home is better for most people. It saves hours of commuting and gives workers more control over their day. Productivity studies show people get just as much done at home.
SPEAKER B: I disagree. The office is where collaboration and mentorship happen. Young employees learn by watching colleagues, and that's hard to do over video calls. A hybrid model misses the spontaneity that sparks ideas.
SPEAKER A: Fair point, but not every job needs that. Many roles are focused and quiet, and those workers are far more efficient at home without office distractions.
SPEAKER B: Perhaps, but I worry that fully remote work weakens team culture over time. People who never meet in person tend to feel less connected to the company.

Bookshelf assembly instructions (Model BB-40)

Parts list:
- 2 side panels (A)
- 4 shelves (B)
- 1 back panel (C)
- 8 screws (D)
- 8 dowels (E)
- 1 hex key (F)

Steps:
1. Lay the back panel flat and insert the four dowels into its top holes.
2. Attach the side panels to the back panel by pressing them onto the dowels.
3. Slide each shelf into the side grooves, starting from the bottom.
4. Secure the shelves with the screws, using the hex key.
5. Stand the unit upright and fix the back panel with the remaining screws.

sections.title: Reading Part 3 · Reading for Information
sections.instructions: Read the article and answer the questions.
sections.passage:
Sleep is not a luxury; it is a biological necessity. While you sleep, your brain consolidates memories, clears waste products, and repairs tissue. Most adults need between seven and nine hours each night, yet surveys show that nearly one in three gets less than seven.

Chronic sleep loss is linked to a range of health problems, including weakened immunity, high blood pressure, and difficulty concentrating. It also affects appetite-regulating hormones, which is why poor sleep is associated with weight gain.

To improve sleep, experts recommend a consistent schedule, a cool and dark bedroom, and avoiding screens for at least an hour before bed. Caffeine and alcohol can both disrupt sleep quality, even when they do not prevent falling asleep.

Even small changes help. Going to bed and waking at the same time every day is one of the most effective steps you can take, because it trains your body's internal clock.

questions.explanation: Poor sleep affects appetite-regulating hormones, linked to weight gain.

sections.title: Reading Part 4 · Reading for Viewpoints

sections.passage:
Electric Cars: A Step Forward
By Priya N.

Electric vehicles are essential to cutting urban air pollution. They produce no tailpipe emissions, cost less to run than petrol cars, and their batteries are improving every year. As charging networks expand, range anxiety will fade, and cities will become quieter and healthier.

Electric Cars: A Costly Distraction
By Tom R.

Electrics are not the green miracle they appear to be. Mining lithium and cobalt damages ecosystems, and most electricity still comes from fossil fuels. Meanwhile, public transit, cycling, and walking deliver bigger environmental gains for far less money. We should invest in those first, not in expensive cars for the few.

sections.title: Writing Task 1 · Email
sections.instructions: Write an email based on the task below.

writingTask.title: Writing an Email
writingTask.scenario: You recently bought a blender online, but it arrived with a cracked jug. Write an email to the store's customer service.
instructions: Explain what you ordered and when it arrived.
Describe the damage and how it affects use.
Say what you would like the store to do.
Keep a polite and professional tone.
writingTask.sampleAnswer: Dear Customer Service, I am writing about order #4471, a NutriBlend Pro blender, which arrived on Tuesday. Unfortunately, the glass jug was cracked when I opened the box, so the blender leaks and cannot be used safely. I would appreciate a replacement jug or a full refund. Please let me know how to return the damaged item. Thank you for your help.

criteria.label: Content
criteria.note: Covers the order, the damage, and the requested resolution.

sections.title: Writing Task 2 · Survey Response
sections.instructions: Write a response to the survey questions below.

writingTask.title: Responding to Survey Questions
writingTask.scenario: Your city is planning to turn a vacant downtown lot into either a public park or a parking garage. Complete the survey explaining which option you prefer and why.
instructions: Give at least two reasons for your choice.
Suggest one improvement to your preferred option.
writingTask.sampleAnswer: I strongly prefer a public park. First, our neighbourhood has little green space, and a park would give families a safe place to gather. Second, parks attract visitors to nearby shops and cafes, which helps local businesses. To improve the idea, I suggest adding a small playground and a few shaded benches. Thank you for asking residents for their views.

criteria.label: Content
criteria.note: States a clear position with supporting reasons and a suggestion.

criteria.label: Tone
criteria.note: Appropriate for a public survey response.

criteria.label: Organization
criteria.note: Ideas are grouped and easy to follow.

criteria.label: Language
criteria.note: Full sentences with accurate grammar and spelling.

sections.title: Speaking Task 1 · Giving Advice
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 1: Giving Advice
speakingTask.scenario: Your friend is moving to a new city for a job and is nervous about making friends. Give your friend advice on how to settle in and meet people.
tips: Give two or three specific, practical suggestions.
Use a warm and encouraging tone.
Speak for about 60 seconds.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: If I were you, I would start by joining a local club or fitness class, because shared activities make it much easier to meet people. I would also suggest volunteering on weekends, since it connects you with neighbours who share your values. Finally, give yourself time — new friendships usually take a few months to form.

sections.title: Speaking Task 2 · Talking about a Personal Experience
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 2: Talking about a Personal Experience
speakingTask.scenario: Describe a time you learned something new that changed how you do things. Include what you learned and how it affected you.
tips: Set the scene briefly.
Explain what you learned and why it mattered.
Use past tenses consistently.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: Last year I learned how to cook from scratch, and it completely changed my routine. Before, I relied on takeout and ready meals, but learning a few basic techniques made cooking faster and much cheaper. Now I plan meals every Sunday and genuinely enjoy it.

sections.title: Speaking Task 3 · Describing a Scene
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 3: Describing a Scene
speakingTask.scenario: Describe a busy marketplace you have visited. Include what you saw, heard, and felt.
tips: Use descriptive vocabulary and the five senses.
Organize your description clearly.
Keep the listener engaged with specific details.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: The market was a riot of colour and noise. Stalls were piled with bright fruit, and vendors shouted their prices over the crowd. The air smelled of grilled meat and fresh herbs, and everywhere people were bargaining, laughing, and hurrying past with full bags.

sections.title: Speaking Task 4 · Making Predictions
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 4: Making Predictions
speakingTask.scenario: Predict how technology will change education in the next twenty years. Give at least two predictions and explain them.
tips: Use language of prediction such as will and likely.
Give a reason for each prediction.
Structure your answer with clear points.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: I think technology will make education far more personal. Software will likely adapt lessons to each student's pace, so nobody is held back or left behind. I also predict that virtual classrooms will become common, letting students in remote areas learn from expert teachers anywhere in the world.

sections.title: Speaking Task 5 · Comparing and Persuading
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 5: Comparing and Persuading
speakingTask.scenario: A friend cannot decide whether to buy a house or keep renting. Persuade your friend to choose one option and explain why it is the better choice.
tips: State your position clearly.
Give at least two advantages of your chosen option.
Use persuasive language.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: I would tell my friend to keep renting for now. Buying a house ties up a lot of money in a down payment, while renting leaves you free to move for work and avoids repair costs. Renting also gives you time to save a larger deposit and buy a place you truly love later.

sections.title: Speaking Task 6 · Dealing with a Difficult Situation
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 6: Dealing with a Difficult Situation
speakingTask.scenario: A coworker has been taking credit for your work in team meetings. Explain what you would say and do to handle the situation.
tips: Describe the steps you would take calmly.
Explain what you would say to the coworker.
Suggest how you would raise the issue professionally.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: I would first speak to my coworker privately and explain, politely but clearly, that the work was mine and that I would appreciate being acknowledged. If it continued, I would mention my contribution directly in the next meeting and, if needed, discuss the pattern with our manager using examples and records of my work.

sections.title: Speaking Task 7 · Expressing Opinions
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 7: Expressing Opinions
speakingTask.scenario: Should all students be required to learn a second language in school? State your opinion and support it with reasons.
tips: Give a clear opinion.
Support it with two or three reasons.
Use appropriate connectors.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: I believe every student should study a second language. It improves memory and problem-solving, and it opens doors to other cultures and careers. In a connected world, being bilingual is a real advantage, and starting early in school makes it much easier to reach fluency.

sections.title: Speaking Task 8 · Describing an Unusual Situation
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 8: Describing an Unusual Situation
speakingTask.scenario: You arrive at the airport and realize you forgot your passport at home. Describe what you would do, step by step.
tips: Describe your actions in a logical order.
Use clear sequencing words such as first and next.
Stay calm and practical.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: First, I would stay calm and check my bag one more time in case I had missed it. Then I would call a family member and ask them to bring the passport to the airport if there was time. If not, I would speak to the airline desk immediately to ask about rescheduling my flight and what identification alternatives they accept.
